en:
Heyyy, what's up?
How's it going?
Uh, yeah, we're here to investigate the - [i]murder[/i] - of Magnus Mortuga.
[h]Oh,[/h] yeah - major bummer, honestly - he was a pretty standup guy.
Dirk - you didn't tell us your surname.
Oh right - sorry.

Dirk Dansom.
[h]Actor.[/h]
I mean, you know, sure - kind of an oddball, but like, in a good way? You know, I mean, he-
So - yeah anyway... um, hi! And, uh - what can I do for you folks?

He's adorable.
Can we keep him?

No.
You'd forget to feed him.
I would, yeah.
Uh... it's going good. I think.
Awesome, yeah - um, I'm Dirk by the way. Who are you guys?
I'm... Grimoire, and this is Sally-
Ohh cool, cool - so - you're the detectives?

So - Dirk... you're an actor?
What kind?

Nice.
Anything I've seen?
Well, it's called [i]'Hex of the Helmsman'[/i].
Oh - you've seen it?
No, but I read the book.
Oh man, the book is gnarly - I'm not usually one for reading, but I actually finished it. The whole thing!
Congrats.
Was your movie a success, Dirk?
Yeah man, it's making mega bucks.
-are you going to make a sequel?
And, what - you're taking your vacation on a [i]submarine[/i] while you wait?
Well, you know, they wanna move on that ASAP but, uh, we're not ready to start filming yet.
No, I'm just here tagging along here with Wirman.
He wanted to take a trip out here and I figured - you know, the more the merrier!
[i]Markus Mordoom?[/i]
The author's a stand-up dude, too.

J. D. Wirman?
You know him?
Uh - yeah! He's sitting right over there.
I bet.
I play the Helmsman.
You should go talk to him. Super friendly. [i]Loves[/i] meeting new people.
Oh, well, uh, so for [h]ages[/h] I just did commercials-
-and then about a year ago I finally got cast in a movie.
Honestly? Mixed bag.
Listen - if you're not careful, it'll [h]get[/h] you. No for real.
You seem to be holding out.
Ha, well thanks - you know, so far so good!
Dirk, you're basically just a [i]passenger[/i], am I right?
You don't have a - [i]job[/i] here on the submarine...?
Uh, well - you know, I set myself [i]personal[/i] goals.
Like what?
I got Sinthia's, Gripp's, [i]Tadpole's[/i] - oh man, [i]that[/i] one took some doing, she does [i]not[/i] like to share personal info, lemme tell you...
It's lucky they still had this room free... you ended up with pretty nice living quarters.
Hahaha, I guess! I never really thought about it!
How long has it been?
Wirman and I arrived a couple weeks ago. We're the most recent arrivals, aside from Mariana.
Like, um - well - I was trying find out everyone's [i]birthday.[/i]
-all kinds of people I'd normally never rub shoulders with, you know-
What do you make of the Mortuga submarine?
Man, this place is [h]wild[/h] - it's like something out of a weird old book.
Nobody back home is going to believe [h]any[/h] of it.

[i]Mortuga[/i], though?
[i]Brick wall[/i], dude. He would [i]not[/i] give me the goods.
So, I love meeting all the weirdos that ended up down here-
How d'you like living here?
-but man is it [h]dark.[/h] There's no sun, no day, no night - you barely even feel the time passing.
Yeah - Wirman and I left our room, went through the mess hall, and towards the store room at the end.
It was unlocked. Sym was standing in the doorway...
I tried to help Sym, you know - pull her away.
Although, I don't think he noticed the person outside.
Luckily Tadpole showed up a short while later, and she kinda took charge.
...Gripp and Sinthia showed up next...
...then Mariana...
...then Zephyr.
Tadpole wanted to know what had happened, but nobody had any answers for her.
Sym and Sinthia left first...
...then Wirman...
So - yeah, I went back to my room.
...then me and Mariana - we left around the same time.
And, uh... you know that's all I got.
-at some point, I got curious what time it was, so I looked at my watch.
But as I was looking at it, it freaked out, the hands moving all over...
...like they were trying to point in all directions at once - if that makes any sense?
[i]Wirman[/i], though - he just stood there, staring. Didn't look away once.
It was like he was trying to commit it to memory or something...
It woke Wirman up, too.
Mortuga was on the floor, totally dead.
Sorry, what?
Outside the submarine. I saw someone swim down past the window.
I wasn't sure [h]what[/h] to do, to be honest.
Okay... what did you do next?
Couldn't tell who it was, though.
It was bad vibes all around.
Wirman was there already - he'd gone straight back to work.
Can I - stop talking now?
I got woken up when the submarine did a weird kinda movement - like a sudden tilt.
So, yeah, we were both sitting there, [i]awake[/i], not sure what's going on-
Anyway, I didn't have any more time to think about it - since then we heard this scream.
Which part suggests Dirk has been planning to kill someone?
Do we have evidence to suggest Dirk has been planning to kill someone?
Do we have audio evidence to suggest Dirk has been planning to kill someone?
How does Dirk contact people outside the submarine?
What device would Dirk use to contact people outside the submarine?
Which part shows the correspondance between Dirk and Mr Van De Peer?
Which part suggests Dirk might have wanted to take other acting jobs?
Did we learn anything about Dirk's contract with the movie studio?
Did we read an interview referencing Dirk's contract with the movie studio?
Tell me, Dirk - have you ever been involved in the planning... of a [h]murder?[/h]

[Present Clue]
Wooden Pipe
Eh. A little from column A, a little from column B.
You said yourself - the studio wanted to make at least three more Markus Mordoom movies.
So you're stuck in that lousy contract for several years...
So... if Wirman kills off the character in the books - that would stop the studio making more movies...?
I'm not convinced that would actually [h]work,[/h] but okay.
The point is, now that I'm a known actor, I could be making more money with a different studio. A [h]lot[/h] more.
But I [h]can't[/h] let it get out that I wanted the Mordoom character to be killed off.
Everyone's gonna take it the wrong way. They'll call me... greedy... and ungrateful...
Hey. Listen. Why don't we just kill him?
Look, you gotta understand, killing off Mordoom isn't just about me.
He's not enjoying writing the books anymore.
The whole thing became just this awful burden.
Hm...
And hey, besides... you know-
So, uh... who are you planning to kill, Dirk?
You know, those guys who pay your salary?
So, they sent me to keep an eye on him. Maybe even - steer him in the right direction a little bit.
The person you're talking to in the recording must be Wirman-
-you're suggesting he should kill off the Mordoom character in his next book.
...and you ended up with a bad deal.
Possibly just because you didn't have much negotiating power - since you weren't famous yet.
...unless you can somehow ensure the next movie is the last one.
A way out...?
I was also trying to help Wirman - he's been looking for a way out too.
I'm sure he'd be happier if he could just - be done with it.
Uh - maybe killing the main character would actually make for an [i]interesting[/i] story. D'you ever consider that?

[Present Clue]
Movie Magazine
...we might just have to assume this is a recording of you planning to kill [h]Magnus Mortuga.[/h]
I figured, surely meeting the real Mortuga would help with my portrayal of [i]Mordoom[/i] in the next movie.
So, he set me up with a way to turn my cell phone into a kinda... heavy duty satellite phone.
Hang on.
In fact, I don't think it was your own idea at all.
Sorry. But I can't tell you.
That's because you didn't pay your network bill in a timely manner.
That's because your phone is broken.
J.D. Wirman, the author.
Vincent Van De Peer, the movie producer.
You want to quit acting and become a writer.
You hate the character and think he's boring.
If he dies, we're both free, right?
That helps both of us!
If he dies, we're both free, right?
I know that sounds mondo suspicious, but - I just flat out can't say any more about it.
That helps both of us!
Come on, I know you don't have any better ideas.
If you're not going to elaborate...
Come on man, that's way off, why would I want to kill Mortuga? I admire the guy, he's fascinating!!
I came to the submarine to [h]meet[/h] him, not murder him.
I thought you only came to submarine because you were tagging along with Wirman?
I mean, yeah - it was Wirman who wanted to come to Silkwirm and, you know, find the submarine, but-
Wait - I'm falling behind - Dirk, why would [h]you[/h] want to research Mortuga?
-I figured if I came [i]with[/i] him, I could meet this real [i]guy[/i] - the real Mortuga. You know... for research.

[Mind Game]
Magnus Mortuga / was the original inspiration for / Markus Mordoom, / the character Dirk plays in the movie.
Right. So, look, I had this idea-
Like I said, [i]research![/i] You hear about actors doing that kind of thing, don't you?
So - that was [h]your[/h] idea? Your [h]own personal plan[/h], to come with Wirman to the submarine?
Um, yeah, but I don't like the way you [i]phrased[/i] that, it sounds like you're leading up to something or-
Yeah, I don't believe that's why you came here with Wirman.
There's clearly a third party involved. Someone or something that we haven't mentioned yet...

[Mind Game]
The movie production company / asked you to spy on / J. D. Wirman / and report back.
It seems like you're basically here as an informant for the Wit and Whimsy production company.
[i]Spy[/i] on Wirman? No way, you've got it all wrong.
Besides - how am I supposed to report back to Wit and Whimsy?
Th-they're hundreds of miles away, and we're floating out here in the middle of the ocean.

[Present Clue]
Cell Phone
This is your cell phone, right?
Yeah, but it doesn't get any [i]signal[/i] out here, not even standing on deck.
It's quickly running out of battery, too...

Hm. No battery, and no signal.
What if I said you had a way around [h]both[/h] those problems?

[Clue Attach Game]
Cell Phone + Strange Device
I think this weird raygun-looking thing... is actually a custom antenna for your phone.

I'd imagine it doubles as a battery charger, too.
Pretty convenient.
-I mean look, you plugged it in, but the battery still isn't charging, and I'm [h]still[/h] not getting any network signal.
Because the custom antenna thing is broken.
Because your phone is broken.
Because you didn't pay your network bill in a timely manner.
Why isn't the cell phone getting any network signal?
Bro, I don't know what you're basing this on-
That's because the custom antenna thing is broken.
Oh, for real? Oh, man, it doesn't [h]look[/h] broken?
I'm pretty sure it got waterlogged after someone dumped it in the bilge water.
[h]That's[/h] where it was? No wonder I couldn't find it.
Um... I mean-

Okay. Whatever, you got me.
Consider me fully [h]got.[/h]
You know, this thing doesn't look like any kind of retail model... more like a one-off bit of custom engineering.
I'm guessing the production company issued it to Dirk specifically for this journey.
Probably when they realised he'd be out in the ocean and might need some help getting a phone signal...
Yeah, so - Mr Van De Peer really didn't want me going [i]'off grid'...[/i]

[h]Bro.[/h]
Not cool.
-and what did Mr Van De Peer want you to keep him [h]informed[/h] about, exactly?
Dirk doesn't have to admit to anything else - all the evidence we need is right here.

[Present Clue]
Cell Phone
There's a handful of outgoing messages, from you to Vincent Van De Peer.
Specifically, they're all updates on Wirman's progress with his novel.
...look - the studio was worried Wirman was just gonna disappear without ever finishing the book.

The right direction?
-in terms of the story?
Yeah, so - the movie studio has this grand plan - they want to make [i]three more[/i] Markus Mordoom movies - [h]at least.[/h]
Why would you come right out and attack me like that?
And, so, they really need Wirman to have his books play out to support that plan.
Three more movies, huh? Sounds like quite a commitment.

Yeah, I mean... yeah.
It is.
It would take years.
Interesting...
I think we may have finally looped back around to the question at hand.
Let's listen to this again, shall we?
Hey. Listen. Why don't we just kill him?
Dirk - I think I've finally worked out who you wanted to kill.
Markus Mordoom, the fictional character.
Vincent Van De Peer, the movie producer.
J.D. Wirman, the author.
Who did Dirk want to kill?
Markus Mordoom, the fictional character.
Hey. Come on, dude.
Why would I want to kill off Mordoom? That's my character, my - my job!
You want to be free to take other acting jobs instead.
You hate the character and think he's boring.
You want to quit acting and become a writer.
Why would Dirk want to kill off Markus Mordoom?
Do you deny it?
You want to be free to take other acting jobs instead.
Let's take a look at the cell phone one more time.

[Present Clue]
Cell Phone
There's an email in here offering you a big role in an upcoming movie...
...and another email from your agent, reminding you that you're not free to take it - and won't be for several years.
From what I gather, you signed a pretty lousy contract with Wit and Whimsy, and now you-
Okay, hang on, sorry - but how would [h]you[/h] know anything about my contract?
Well, I don't know the fine details, but I did get a general sense of it...
It seems to me like your co-star soaked up most of the budget for the movie...
Possibly because you were too keen to sign whatever contract they gave you.
I am [h]officially[/h] living the dream, how many people can say they're an action figure?

[i]Mint[/i] condition...?
I really wouldn't say-
Huh... do you have the whole set? Looks like there are [i]two[/i] other figures in the series?
Yeah, you know, they told me if I leave it in the box it'll be worth way more in the future.
Oh, no, they only gave me this one. My co-star Julie has the other two.

I'll admit it.
I'm jealous.
You carry this thing around everywhere you go, Dirk?
Of course - but I'm super duper careful to keep it in mint condition.
Apparently Gripp ended up on the submarine because he crashed his balloon over the ocean?
Maybe he just got caught in a storm.
Oh yeah...  I didn't think about that.
I mean, it's a great story, but...
You don't think it's true?
Gripp's pretty smart, in fact, he might even be the smartest guy on the submarine.
...I just don't see him crashing his balloon like that.
What's that?
Oh, let me guess - it's locked and you can't work out how to open it?
Right again.
Ha - classic.
-okay but, for real, you [h]gotta[/h] let me know when you get it open cos now I'm [h]super[/h] curious.
You've never seen it before?
Nope - is it Mortuga's?
Good guess.
Yeah, it has his vibes for sure.
Holy moly, look at that!
I know. That werewolf looking guy is really-
-is that Tadpole with [h]long hair?[/h]
Uh - yeah, maybe?
She never told me about that! It's a strong look.
Gripp must have [i]really[/i] steady hands, working with all those small parts, huh? I could never.
Oh, yeah, I've seen that in the control room.
I thought maybe Sinthia was going to wear it? Like after she became captain?
I think it might be too big for her.

Oh yeah.
I wonder if it's on purpose.
Maybe he just never bothered to decide on one.

Right.
-doesn't seem like he was a... [i]paperwork[/i] kinda guy.
Yeah... guess not.
...Huh. That's kinda weird.
What?
He doesn't have a signature - Mortuga. He writes his name differently every time.
Where does Zephyr [h]find[/h] this stuff?
Huh. Some of the listings in here, the prices are in [h]ounces[/h]... and there's a symbol?
It's the alchemical symbol for gold.
For real?
Man, is Zephyr like secretly [h]super rich?[/h]
I'm pretty sure they don't sell this magazine at my local newstand.
...maybe on mail-order...
...I think it's more of a black market thing.
So - Sinthia hired you to solve the murder, huh?
[h]Good question.[/h] Grimoire, how much [h]did[/h] we make from the Tangle Tower case?
Uh, well - you know...
You never secured the payment, huh?
[i]Extenuating[/i] circumstances, uh, being what they [i]were...[/i]
Pretty much.
How much do you charge? Is it like a day rate, or - what?
Oh, uh - it, uh - you know it - it depends.
-just ballpark it, how much did you make from the last case you solved?
This is yours, Dirk?
We literally found it in the pocket of your tuxedo.
How d'you know for sure it's [i]my[/i] tuxedo?
Dirk. Show me one other living soul on this submarine that could even [h]conceivably[/h] own a tuxedo.
No... I don't like this at [h]all...[/h]
Or what - Mortuga forced her to sign it?
I don't really see the problem. Sinthia wanted to be captain, and now she's captain.
Whoa, wait - [h]this[/h] is the contract Sinthia signed to become captain??

Seems that way.
What's the problem?
I guess.

Why not?
You think she misread it?
No, it's not that-
She shouldn't have signed it.
Man... Mortuga really was an odd duck, wasn't he?
Maybe, yeah.
Whoa... I wonder where it is now??
Hard to say, since we don't know what we're looking for. But - [h]somewhere[/h] on the submarine, I guess.
Not neccessarily, someone could've thrown it into the ocean!
Oh, great.
I mean, who [i]owns[/i] something like this?? What's it even [i]for?[/i]
It used to be locked, so I think he kept something inside it.
Oh, what - and it got [h]stolen?[/h] The thing - whatever it was?
Hey, wow. Uh, did Tadpole give you that?

It would make sense...
Although the woman in the photo looks a [i]little[/i] different.
[h]So what?[/h] It's a free country!
I guess she dyes it green nowadays?
No, we found it in the bilge. You think it belongs to her?
Nah, it's [h]gotta[/h] be hers, you're right about the photo, though - her hair is brown, here...
Dr Z told me this is a [i]'Dream Helmet'?[/i]
No time, bro, gotta optimize that sleep cycle, you know - [i]if you're dreaming, you're not resting.[/i]
You're insane.
Ha - little bit.
Have you tried it out?
Nope. I don't dream.
[h]What?[/h] Yes you [i]do.[/i]
I don't get it.
Really?
See - this is my point! He [h]hides[/h] it!

What's not to get?
It's a cane with a face!
Okay, so - for real, Gripp's actually, like, [h]super[/h] smart.
[i]W-why?[/i] Why bother with the - the cane, and the whole persona?
What d'you mean?
Well, it's pristine, but - stuff like that doesn't look so hot when it's brand new.
On our [i]movie[/i], we had a guy who roughed up all the outfits, made them look [i]lived-in[/i], you know.
So this photo is the first time Sinthia's mom wore that jacket?
Hm.
-is that Sinthia's mom??
Yeah, I think so.
That jacket is something [h]else![/h]
It... could do with a bit of [i]ageing[/i], though.
What a babe.
...I dunno, wasn't he kind of a gloomy loner?
Hahaha - chicks eat that [h]up,[/h] man.
Uh... I don't think so, she-
This Mortuga's [i]girlfriend[/i] or something?
I mean... yeah.
[h]Of course[/h] he'd land a girl like this. [h]Of course![/h]
Dirk, you're a [i]movie[/i] kinda guy - is this your projector?
What's on it?
Uhh, [h]that[/h] is, though.
Oh, it's just like, um - a bit of a scene... a [i]daily[/i], you know.
Where'd you get it from?
It was a gift from the studio - lil' souvenir.
Where did you lose it?
I dunno, Mess Hall, probably? Where did you [i]find[/i] it?
It was in the hollowed out stomach of a do-

It was in a cabinet.
Normal - cabinet.
Oh! Okay. Cool.
So, uh... can I have it back?
Nope! Not mi-
The film reel?
Yup. I thought I'd lost it! I guess I [i]did[/i], huh.
-is that a [i]crystal ball?[/i]
It's genius.
-I think it's made of glass.
Right - but - a crystal ball in the sense that it's a magic ball you look into and see your future or whatever?

Oh.
Yeah, I guess.
Why don't [h]you[/h] look into it - you'll see yourself solving the murder - and then you'll know who did it.
Someone lose an eye?
Oh.
Uh, s'got a weird smell.
So?
So maybe try asking Mariana about it, she's got a [i]wicked[/i] sense of smell - like a [i]dog.[/i]
I'm serious!
It's not real.
Hey! It's Sym's necklace locket thing.
Unless you decide it's related to the [i]murder[/i]. Then you'd be all over it, I bet.
Dang. Called out.
Any idea what she keeps in there?
It's not really my business.
It might get a better signal up in the control room, or up on deck.
Down here you get nothing - the walls are way too thick.
...a radio? What's the range on that thing?
No idea. I'm pretty sure it's broken anyway.
Uh, no - generally speaking you [i]do not[/i] read another dude's fanmail.
What makes you think it's fanmail?
Wirman read that thing a [h]hundred[/h] times over on the journey down here.
I just figured... must be something nice, you know?
Oh, hey, you found Wirman's letter.
Have you read it?
Hey, so - remind me what a [i]Hex[/i] is again?
I... I was hoping that would clear up what a [i]Hex Bottle[/i] was, but no dice.
Didn't you [h]just[/h] make a movie called [i]'Hex of the Helmsman'[/i]??
Right, right, but - look - I'm bad with learning what the made up words mean.

It's... not a made up word.
A Hex is a magic spell - kinda like a curse.
Or it can mean [i]six[/i] - as in hexagon.
Ahh, gotcha... okay...

Whoa, this is a first [h]edish!![/h]
Who's [h]is[/h] this?
...okay maybe I do want that.
I assume you've read it, Dirk?
Of course, dude - first thing I did when I landed the part in the movie.
What did you think?
Loved it. I'd never thought about the sea so much in my whole life.
It's almost like... the ocean in the book... it represents something... bigger, you know?
It's mine.
You gonna get Wirmo to sign it?
No... I hadn't planned on it.
He'd do it if you asked! I bet he'd even do a little [i]doodle[/i] on the inside cover.
Huh. Who's that little grim reaper guy in the drawing?
I'm not sure. You recognise it?
It does seem kinda familiar, for - some reason?
That is one [h]old[/h] document.
Huh. I guess it runs in perpetuity.
What about if you ripped it in half?
Ha, you know what - I found that doesn't actually do jack?
No, I know - it works in the movies, but in real life, voiding a contract is a more [i]complex procedure.[/i]
Well that's no fun.
I'd be surprised if it hasn't expired by now...
Expired?
Yeah, things like this normally have an agreed upon-
Oh, no - there's no date.
What does it [h]do??[/h]
I thought it was a bell.
Only it doesn't actually ring, so... not really a bell, but-
Nah I think it's some kinda... [i]mechanism.[/i]
The bit sticking out the bottom looks a bit like a screwdriver. Don't you think?
Hey, I didn't know Sym had a stunt dummy.
It's not a stunt-
She planning to do a scene where she falls off a cliff into a crocodile-infested river?
When the stunt is that dangerous, and the stunt guy refuses to do it - you use the dummy.

[h]'HER.'[/h]
Ha. Deliberately vague title. Love it.
That's my bottle!

What?
Uh - really?
Yeah, that's one of my non-alcoholic beers.
Course, someone's waxed up the top and put a whole bunch of green stuff on the bottom...
Hey, that's pretty cute.
I thought it was just, like, you know - [i]toytown[/i] or whatever.
Never mind.
Do you recognise any of the buildings?
Oh - is it supposed to be something specific??
Someone drop their perfume...?
...bummer, that stuff can get [i]expensive.[/i]
Lookin' good, Julie.
Right, you're the title character, but, there's uh - only one name at the top.
Oh... you noticed?
Uh - Julie was already a big name, so... you know, she got her name on the poster.
Seems unfair.
...well, I'm sure when they make the sequel, Dirk's name will be front and centre.
R-right.
-you're featured in the interview, though!
Uh, right at the... end.
And they spelled your name wrong.
Are we done looking at the magazine?
I assume this is yours, Dirk.
Yeah - I let the kids borrow it, since there weren't a lot of other magazines on board...
I noticed on the back - there's an advert for your movie.
Yup. That's me on the left, all dolled up as Markus Mordoom, the [i]titular[/i] helmsman.
Hey, the guy who wrote this review has the same name as...
I'm - I'm not sure if I'm allowed to say.
As - who?
Oh, a combination lock - let me try...
Easy. It was her birthday.
Huh!
It belongs to Madam Tadpole, but it's locked.
What's that?
Yep. Got it.
How did you know the code?
What's the deal with those holes along the sides?
Why would a submarine need a sail??
They're from when it was a sail.
A big chest of gold doubloons, you think?
Oh, sweet, treasure map.
-It doesn't specifically [h]say[/h] it's a treasure map.
Oh man, that would be [i]awesome...[/i]
Although, thinking about it, d'you think anywhere still takes doubloons?
Dude, there's a big red X. You gotta assume that's a treasure.
Hey - is that the [i]Queen Serena?[/i]
-is [h]that[/h] what the ship's called?
No - that's the name of the ship in the [h]novel.[/h] And in Dirk's movie, too. I'm guessing.
I got to steer a big wheel like this in my movie.
Mine didn't have that red metal bit, though.
Also mine was up on the aft deck, not, you know, indoors in a control room.
It's a map - of Silkwirm?
I don't know much about the town, you'd be better off asking someone else.
Ah!
Well, whatever it is, I think it's broken.
Wait, [h]really?[/h]
I mean - [i]oh... what a shame.[/i]
You know what this is, Dirk?
Um... [i]laser gun?[/i]
A laser gun.
I'm glad Sinthia took my advice.
What advice?
She was looking super tense, so I told her to pick up a hobby. Arts and crafts is a good choice.
Oh, you found my tablets?

term: Conversation/Sally Topic 12 ...and a Thief/Section ds50 Choice Question
en: Mortuga tightly shut the bulkhead door from the inside...
They came in via the Captain's Cabin - you know, through the hole in the floor?
He had a key, he would've locked it!
Definitely - since he'd've rearranged it like [i]we[/i] just did - moving the desk and the rug to reveal the hole...
So the culprit would've needed the eyeball key...
Yeah - I'm pretty sure Mortuga [i]did[/i] take the key into the Illusion Theatre.
Remember how it smelled kinda weird? That's the [i]bilgewater smell.[/i]
No - it didn't happen by accident.

term: Conversation/Sally Topic 12 ...and a Thief/Section ds64 Choice Question
en: Why did the eyeball key roll across the floor and into the vent?
Making the submarine surface tilts the [i]front[/i] end up, and the [i]back[/i] end down...
[i]Mortuga's blood[/i] - it pooled out first, but then started running down towards the bilge vent...
It steadily goes down... but then later, it suddenly goes back [i]up[/i] again!
So the moon vial rolled right off Mortuga's desk and through the hole in the floor...
Once the culprit had the key, they could let themselves into the Captain's Cabin...
They climbed down the rope, through the hole...
Although, to get out - they'd need to climb back [i]up[/i] the bell rope.
...and into this room - where they were free to take the contents of the cauldron for themselves.
...and after that, all they had to do was cover the hole back up with the rug and the desk.
Anything else?

term: Conversation/Sally Topic 12 ...and a Thief/Section ds78 Choice Question
en: Evidence that the submarine was surfaced shortly after the murder.
The cauldron was [i]always[/i] empty.
The culprit didn't [i]need[/i] to use that door.
How?
But then he died - in a [i]locked[/i] room. So how did someone [i]else[/i] get hold of it?
-it fell into the bilge?
The culprit used a magnet.
So the eyeball key just [i]happened[/i] to roll across the floor and into the vent?
The culprit tilted the submarine.
A phenomenon observed at the crime scene...
A clue found in the control room...
A clue found at the crime scene...
It is I, Sinthia Seafoam! [h]Fearless[/h] Captain of the Mortuga Submarine.
Aha! Then [h]you[/h] must be Detective Grimoire.
Uh - correct. Yes.
[i]The world's greatest detective[/i], here, on my submarine-

[i]The world's-[/i]
No no I'm not the world's greatest, just [h]a[/h] detective.
Uh, she was probably talking about [h]me?[/h]
Now, I assume you've come to make your official report?
Let's hear it - I'm a busy woman, you know!
Slow down there, Miss Seafoam.
We just came in here to [i]question[/i] you - since you're one of the suspects.
But [h]I[/h] hired you!
What...? Really?
Yeah, no - that doesn't get you off the hook, I'm afraid.
[i]Ugh.[/i] This is [h]so[/h] totally unfair.
Hey, so - thanks for finally letting us in.
You know, I have to say, that [i]really was[/i] pretty unhelpful-
Hi. I'm Sally.
So... how'd you end up as the new captain?
[i]-it's all above board, okay??[/i]
I didn't say it wasn't.
Sinthia, what were you [i]before[/i] you became captain? D'you have any credentials?
Fifteen years experience as a nautical engineer and shipyard mechanic. Family business.
You don't look much older than fifteen [h]now.[/h]

...
I'm [h]eight[/h]een!! [i]Ugh.[/i]
How does an eighteen-year-old end up on a [i]submarine?[/i]
I came by rowing boat.
Correct.
Wait, the rowing boat we saw up on the [i]fore deck?[/i] That's yours?
That's not really what I meant-
...I'll add it to the list.
You should know, it's in bad shape. And it's missing an oar.
So how come you wanted to hire Grimoire?
Because! There's a [h]murderer[/h] in our ranks... and they must be rooted [i]out![/i]
So - what d'you want us to [i]do[/i] exactly?
[h]One[/h] - you will investigate and ascertain the identity of the killer...
[h]Two[/h] - you will return here and report your findings to me.
Three, you go home.

Three, you [h]pay[/h] us.
[h]Four,[/h] we go home.
Three, she pays us, four, we go get [i]ice-cream[/i], [h]five[/h] we go home.
[h]Deal![/h]
Meeting adjourned!
I didn't actually say [i]anything.[/i]
Wait, I didn't-
It's just the way it's meant to [i]be.[/i]
Why did you wanna come to the submarine in the [i]first[/i] place? To become [i]captain?[/i]
Not yet - we'll get there.
How long have you [i]been[/i] here, Sinthia?
I arrived a few weeks before Mr Wirman and Mr Dansom.
Oh, well - Mortuga put me up in the bunk room at the bow end of the ship. I share a room with Sym.
I'm assuming you don't live here in the control room - where do you sleep?
If you arrived before Dirk and Wirman, the other bunk room would've still been empty...
Yeah, I think he wanted to keep that other bunk room vacant.
Huh. Interesting.
I'm not complaining - I really [h]like[/h] sharing with Sym! She's great!
...but Mortuga made you [i]share?[/i]
So, what are you gonna do with the submarine, now that you're captain?
My first order of business - hiring you two!
Sure, I get that. What about [h]afterwards?[/h]
Uhh-
We really can't do anything else until this gets cleared up, you know...
We'll - sail the seven seas! -and have adventures...
You know. That... kinda stuff.
I sought an audience with Magnus Mortuga. I had things I wished to discuss with him!
Like what?
...matters of great importance! Affairs of great significance! Dealings of great-
She's not gonna tell us.
...someone mentioned that Sym was the last person who'd seen Mortuga alive...
Everyone should've been asleep, but suddenly... we were surfacing.
My bunk room's in the bow, and I could feel it tilting up.
I was gonna go check, but then I noticed Sym was wide awake, looking upset.
When I asked, she told me something had gone wrong with the new [i]magic act[/i] she'd set up.
She seemed to agree with that, so I left her and went up to the control room.
I told her she could always take it down, rework it, and then try it again later.
She wanted me to bring Gripp and everyone else and meet her outside the storage room upstairs.
Did he agree to fix it for you?
Yeah... of course. He even said he had a bunch of [i]replacement needles[/i] he could try out.
-and the three of us went up to the store room like Tadpole had asked.
You went straight back to your room?
Uhh, no, I went back up to the control room first.
The control room was empty, but I could see we [i]had[/i] actually surfaced - so I went up onto the fore deck to check.
For what reason?
I was wondering if Mortuga had left any instructions... or any paperwork - I wanted to read the captain's log, too.
Something tells me that's not the whole story.
If you have any other specific questions, I'll uh - field them separately.
That's the whole statement, I swear!!
How could you tell?
When the submarine surfaces, the bow tilts up and the stern tilts down - and diving's the opposite.
The bow is the front.
I knew that!
There wasn't anybody out there either.
I had this weird feeling and really didn't wanna go back to bed, so, I went back to the control room.
I took a closer look at the control panel to see if I could work out why we might've surfaced...
Suddenly, the readings all started to go haywire.
The ship's compass, the needle - it was... uh - malfunctioning.
So, I... pulled it out of its socket.
Yeah, I, uh - figured it would need to be taken for repairs.
So I left the control room, but bumped into Dr Zephyr in the parlor.
He was carrying a little empty bottle made of green glass... I dunno why. I didn't ask.
I woke up when the submarine made an unscheduled maneuver...
I went down the two ladders and towards the engine room - since I wanted Mr Gripp to take a look at the ship's compass.
But then [i]Madam Tadpole[/i] appeared and called out to me.
I went into the Engine Room and gave Mr Gripp the compass - I told him the needle would need replacing.
Anyway, then we went to the cargo hold to fetch Mariana Moon-
I wondered if someone other than Mortuga might be at the wheel...
We went down the corridor - the others were gathered outside the little room at the end...
I... looked through the crowd and saw Captain Mortuga, laying on his back. Dead.
I didn't like where the conversation was heading, so I took Sym and left.
Everyone was trying to work out what had happened...
And... yeah. That's about it.
What allowed Sinthia to officially claim captaincy of the submarine?
What document allowed Sinthia to officially claim captaincy of the submarine?
How was Mortuga's contract made?
How was Mortuga's contract typed?
Do we have evidence to suggest that Sinthia forged Mortuga's signature?
Do we have a record of other signatures, to suggest that Sinthia forged Mortuga's signature on the Contract?
Which part shows the original submarine?
Something that shows Sinthia's connection to the original submarine...
A photograph that shows Sinthia's connection to the original submarine...
Something to show the submarine's original design has been altered...
A diagram to show the submarine's original design has been altered...
What did Sinthia want to give back to Mortuga to undo the purchase of the submarine?
What document did Sinthia want to give back to Mortuga to undo the purchase of the submarine?
Which part shows who ended up owning the Stonetop Inn?
Sinthia's family were constructing...
Sinthia's family were buying...
Sinthia's family were trying to sell...
The deeds show...
...which was known as the Seafoam submarine.
...which was known as the Mortuga submarine.
...which was known as the Silkwirm submarine.
...is now the owner of the Stonetop Inn.
...is now the owner of the Seafoam Submarine.
...is now the owner of Silkwirm-on-sea.
Okay, but you have to admit - the wording on this thing is kind of [i]vague.[/i]
Yeah - the blueprint's from my mother's original design. But as I said, that version was never completed.
I've been trying to update it to show how the submarine looks now - the design changed a bit after Mortuga bought it...
Wait - if Mortuga bought it, then he [h]did[/h] own it.
It wasn't a legitimate purchase. It wasn't my father's to sell.
So - the [i]'recent development'[/i] mentioned in the contract... that was-
That was me, informing Mortuga that his ownership of the submarine was based on an illegitimate purchase.
My intention was to refund his payment and undo the transaction, placing the submarine back into my ownership.
[i]Refund the payment[/i]... you tried to give him his [h]money[/h] back?
It doesn't actually say; [i]'Hi everyone, Mortuga here, Sinthia gets to be captain if I die.'[/i]
Not money. Something else.
The deeds to the Stonetop Inn.
Originally owned by the Stonetop family, until it was passed into the ownership of Magnus Mortuga. And then-
The deeds passed from Mortuga to Donovan Drummond. Sinthia's stepfather.
So [i]that's[/i] how Mortuga paid for the submarine... he sold his house, basically.
I came aboard with the intention of giving the Stonetop Inn back to Mortuga, in exchange for my mother's submarine.
And... that's exactly what I did.
But - did Mortuga actually [h]accept[/h] your offer?
When I first made the proposal... he didn't give me an answer either way.
He looked at the Inn Deeds very closely... read the whole thing, front and back.
Then he handed them back, and told me he'd need some time.
Before I heard anything else about it... he was killed.
But then I found the command contract.
It seemed like he'd decided to accept my proposal after all - and just... not had a chance to tell me.

Let's review, shall we?
Ahem;
After reading it, I could come to only one conclusion;
Obviously, I thought I'd never find out what his decision was...
Wow, I bet he loved that.
We have no evidence.
We have anecdotal evidence.
Sinthia is Mortuga's daughter.
Mortuga sold the submarine to Sinthia before he died.
...Mortuga had the contract typed up - but then never signed it?
Just the way it's meant to be, right. We got it.
[i]'This contract represents an agreement between the two individuals in contention over the ownership and command of the Mortuga submarine.'[/i]
The two individuals - that's you and Mortuga?
Indeed.
But you're not actually named, uh - by [i]name.[/i]
If I may continue?
[i]'For their own safety and privacy, these two people shall only be referred to as Party A and Party B.'[/i]
See? Mortuga was quite a private person. He was just being considerate.
So Mortuga is Party A?

You call it considerate...
I call it [h]convenient.[/h]
Correct.
[i]'Previously, Party A has been considered the legal owner of the Mortuga submarine, and thus its rightful commander.'[/i]
He's clearly talking about himself. It's the Mortuga submarine, after all, and he was the commander.
[i]'However, a recent development has exposed that Party B is in fact the legal owner of this vessel.'[/i]
Party B - that's you?
Affirmative.

[i]'A recent development...'[/i]
There's more of that deliberately vague wording.
I have a question. When exactly did Mortuga [h]write[/h] this contract?
When... [i]exactly?[/i]
I don't actually know-
You don't know when he [i]wrote[/i] it??
Well, it must've been some time after I came aboard the submarine.
I assume it was after I'd... uh - [i]presented my case[/i] to him.
[h]Sinthia[/h] might not know, but we actually have some insight on this-
For one - we know how the contract was written - how it was actually [h]created,[/h] I mean.
It was typed on Wirman's typewriter - so it was made some time [i]after[/i] Wirman arrived.
- and - and Wirman and Dirk arrived after I did! So this gets me off the hook!!
Try not to sound [h]too[/h] relieved. But yeah, this does seem to confirm it.
So, my next question is this: When did you [h]sign[/h] the contract?

Umm... a little while ago?
Some... amount of time ago?
[i]If this conversation gets any more vague I'm going to cry.[/i]
Was it... a [i]day[/i] before the murder? A [i]week?[/i]
Ummm...
Surely it was at [h]some[/h] point before the murder. Otherwise...
I think it might be time to make an accusation.
Ah!!

Such a [h]rude[/h] accusation!
So rude!
Do you have any evidence that it's been forged?
We have evidence in the form of a clue.
We have anecdotal evidence.
We have no evidence.
...is there any evidence that Sinthia forged Mortuga's signature?
We have evidence in the form of a clue.
Sinthia - you became captain after Mortuga died?
I assure you, that is Mortuga's [h]exact[/h] signature.
The captain's log. It's basically a stack of cards printed out by the submarine's control panel.
Each little card has a space for the captain to sign...
...and the most recent card is signed by you, Sinthia. All the rest are signed by Mortuga.
Well. [i]Sort of.[/i]
Uhhh... yeah? It's a perfect match! What's the [i]problem?[/i]
The perfect match [h]is[/h] the problem.
You were too [i]accurate[/i]. If you'd done a worse job, you might've gotten away with it.
Yup - it's just the way it's meant to b-
...what do you mean?
If you look through the cards, Mortuga never signs his name the same way twice.
But the signature on the contract matches one of them [h]exactly.[/h]
Which seems to be proof that you copied it. Or, traced it, or whatever it was.

Oh. Whoops.
Didn't notice that.
I thought it was his signature... why doesn't he have a signature?
So if Sinthia forged the signature, that means...
Right after Mortuga was killed, I went looking to see if he'd written a will.
That's when I found it. Laying inside the little hatch in the control panel.
But, uh - there was something you [i]used[/i] to claim the captaincy? A document?
I grabbed it and hurried back to my room to read it.
That he wrote it about [i]me[/i], but never got a chance to [i]show[/i] it to me.
Remind me why you were so sure it was written about you?
[i]'...a recent development has exposed that Party B is in fact the [h]legal owner[/h] of this vessel.'[/i]
...you're really the [i]legal owner[/i] of the Mortuga submarine?
It was originally the [i]Seafoam[/i] Submarine.
Mortuga sold the submarine to Sinthia before he died.
Sinthia is Mortuga's daughter.
How is Sinthia the legal owner of the Mortuga submarine?
It was originally the [i]Seafoam[/i] Submarine.
Correct.
This was back when it was still being built...
The Seafoam submarine... was never completed.

We got close.
And - then we stopped.
It lay rusting in the shipyard for some time. Mortuga would eventually purchase it from my father.
At which point it was altered, completed, and renamed the [h]Mortuga[/h] submarine.
Altered...?
Hey, do you have a minute? We're, uh - ready to make our report.
What's wrong?
I appreciate your hard work. Truly.
However, I, uh - I think it's time you left.
We didn't even tell you what we found!
I need to go. Everyone's gathering in the mess hall.
I'll resurface the submarine, and you can leave via the fore deck.
So, you're giving [i]up?[/i] You're not gonna - see this [i]through?[/i]
Sorry, but, I just think... maybe-
What??
What - [i]that's just the way it's meant to be?[/i]
People are starting to accuse each other. I don't like it.

Whats with that [i]wheel?[/i] It looks kinda like a shield... does he have that in the [i]movie?
[/i]
He has a wheel in the [i]book[/i]... but it mostly stays attached to his ship - apart from one time it breaks off in a big storm.
Heh. Gripp's not one to give out discounts, huh?
My parents used to shop here, from time to time...
They'd complain that Mr Gripp would charge them [i]full price[/i]. Even though they were locals.
I don't like it.
Like... what if it's something we didn't wanna see??
I think I'd still rather know.
You don't wanna know what's inside?
I do... and I don't.
[i]What if it's bad?[/i]
Bad like how?
[i]Night of a Full Moon...[/i]
Then you'd use a compass. Like a normal person.
My mom taught me how you can use the moon to work out where you are.
Like, if you're sailing on the ocean, and you can see the moon, you can work out which way's North. I think.
What if it's too cloudy?
Uh...
Mhm. Looks like Mr Gripp's already working on fixing it.
Why so many [i]needles?[/i]
The original needle was broken. Mr Gripp said he had a few he could try out as replacements.
This one's the original?
Uh. Yeah.
Looks fine to me. Just put it back in.
Nope! Wouldn't work! It's malfunctioning - it needs to be replaced.
Good! That's - good.
This is the ship's compass? From here in the control room?
It's... just the way it's meant to be.
It's based on the one [i]Mortuga[/i] had. See? The epaulettes are kinda the same.
Oh - I've been wanting to ask someone about this - how come Mortuga's jacket is like - [i]half[/i] a jacket?
Apparently he didn't wanna wear anything on his right shoulder.
Some kind of pain from an old injury, I think.
I have my [i]own[/i] jacket. [i]This[/i] one stays behind glass.
Okay, so what about [i]your[/i] jacket?
So... I notice you're the [i]captain[/i]... but you're not wearing the [i]Captain's Jacket.[/i]
Oh - you found the captain's log.
...with readings from the submarine's movements in the last twenty-four hours...
So the card on the top, that's from the day Mortuga died?
...then the captain signs it and writes about anything noteworthy that happened.
Yeah, I - figured we should have a record of it.
You took over as captain that same [i]night?[/i]
What of it?
Nothing! Just asking...
Sure did.
How does it work?
So, at the end of every day you're supposed to print out one of these little cards...
Huh...
Well, I know it's a big sea serpent that my mom and her best friend fished outta the ocean.
Your [h]mother[/h] found it?
Mhm.
What happened to it? Did she keep it?
Eventually some men came and took it away.
For a while.
Where is it now?
I don't know.
Oh, I know about this one. The Silversnake.
What d'you know about it?
[h]Aha![/h] I see you found my case file.
I gotta ask - did Fiona end up leaving the tower? Or is she still there?
Fifi? Yeah, she and Poppy moved out.
Oh, good for them.
They got a real nice place out in the countryside.
Ahh, that's so nice...
Sure did.
I'm jealous! Hahaha...
Oh, I read all about the [i]Tangle Tower[/i] case in a newspaper.
How come you knew about Grimoire?
I didn't know that got any press. Someone must've sold their story...
Wait, that's a [i]flashlight?[/i]
Sinthia, is this the phone you used to call [i]us?[/i]
No, I used one in the town, when I went to drop off the case file...
I never actually [i]had[/i] my own cell phone - do they all have flashlights like this?
Could be useful - it gets pretty dark down here.
But we've both signed it! So... yep! It's binding!
Where'd it come from?
[i]Mortuga[/i] wrote it. I think he used a typewriter.
And - what - he presented it to you? When?
Well, no, cos he... he died. So.
[h]Yeah[/h], how did you-
No? [i]Great[/i], let's move on.
Any further questions?
There it is - in black and white!
Signed by [i]me[/i], signed by [i]Mortuga...[/i]
Yeah, I can see.
So you think it got opened in the course of the [i]murder?[/i]
I see three possibilities;
One; the cauldron was opened [h]before[/h] the murder.
And three; the cauldron was opened [h]during[/h] the murder.
Two; someone opened the cauldron [h]after[/h] the murder.
Someone other than [i]Mortuga.[/i]
Like... the murder happening and the cauldron opening are [i]one and the same?[/i]
Naturally.
Maybe.
In the case file you said the cauldron had [i]'never been unlocked before'.[/i]
And nobody knew [h]how[/h] to unlock it - except, presumably, Mortuga himself.
[i]Ocean Rescue Divers Association...[/i]
Pardon me for not swimming in the [i]deep freezing ocean.[/i]
Ugh, they'd never let [h]me[/h] in. I can barely even swim.
But you live right by the sea!
We're not sure.
My money's on [h]nothing.[/h]
What does it do?
I'm sure I saw a [i]picture[/i] of this recently - but it looked different...
Where did you see this [i]picture?[/i]
Uh... somewhere in the engine room?
That's your mom?
Yeah. She was the harbormaster.
That's your dad on the right?
Yeah. Stepdad. But yeah.
That's a pretty fancy jacket for a [i]harbormaster[/i]. Looks more like a [i]naval[/i] officer.
Yeah, well. She had a lot of big ideas...
She was super ambitious, always making plans - my dad could barely keep up.
-after a while.
Are you two close?
Mm... not really. We kinda drifted apart after-
I remember one time I went into Mortuga's cabin and he was standing in front of this painting...
...and he had his hand held up to it. Like he was touching it.
Okay, well - he is within his right to do that...
No he wasn't touching the [i]frame[/i], he was touching the painting itself.
I dunno. Might be worth a second look.
Maybe it got knocked and he was straightening it.
Oh - it's Sym's projector.
-is it actually [i]hers?[/i]
Uhh, no, I think she [i]borrowed[/i] it from somebody?
Oh. Sym's Fog ball...
No... I don't think so.
-what's this weird little [i]antenna[/i] thing?
-is that not just part of the design?
Oh?
Seems like the kinda thing she might've fished outta the [i]sea...[/i]
D'you know what this is?
I dunno... does it belong to [i]Madam Tadpole?[/i]
Sym let you see her locket...?
Nah.
Yeah.
I should think [i]not!![/i]
Was it - okay? There wasn't anything bad in there?
It's fine.
Okay. Fine. Good.
Do you know what's inside? Did she ever show you?
No, and I didn't ask. She's allowed to have secrets.
Wait - [i]you[/i] didn't open it, did you?
Yeah.
Nah.

term: Conversation/Sinthia CLUE GoldenLocket/Section ds9 Choice Question
en: You didn't open it, did you?
Does it [h]belong[/h] to you?
Of course, I brought it [i]with[/i] me - that's how I first contacted the submarine from the outside.
You used the radio to contact Mortuga? -and you asked him to let you into the submarine?
Yup!
Wait - so there's a receiver in the control room?

No.
Well - kinda.
So-
You know what, never mind.
Sinthia, this radio looks kinda like [h]you.[/h]
Ahh, you really think so?
Why did she take that as a compliment??
The stamp - that's Governor Fellow. The guy who owned Silkwirm-on-sea.
I didn't know you could own a town.
Well, he [i]acted[/i] like he did. Putting himself on the stamps was the [i]least[/i] of it.
Uh - I don't really [h]want[/h] to know what that is.
Hm. Smells kinda like flowers or something. Weird.
Hey... it's that bottle I saw Dr Zephyr carrying around the submarine.
What about the thing [h]in[/h] the bottle?
So this is what Mr Wirman did after he left town.
You mean like in publishing?
-in [i]anything.[/i]
Why would he need to leave [h]town[/h] to write a book? I feel like you could do that from [i]anywhere.[/i]
It was probably more about making connections.
Silkwirm's a real [i]dead end[/i] if you've got any kind of aspirations.
She's the theatre owner who adopted Sym.
Did Sym [h]like[/h] living with her? -in the theatre?
Mmm... Sym's reluctant to speak ill of her elders...
But I get the sense that Fortuna wasn't very [i]nice[/i] to her.
[i]Baroness Fortuna...[/i]
Who [i]is[/i] she?
Why did you hide it?
I'm allowed to keep stuff under my mattress!
Is it yours...? It doesn't have your name on it.
Hmph. No it [h]doesn't[/h] - that's exactly why I brought it [i]with[/i] me, actually.

No...
I'm done talking.
[i]Inn-deed-[/i]
Oh shut up.
Go on?
You found it, huh.

We did indeed.
